content:
alex: getting alerts — sudden spike in 502/504 for hosted inference in us-west-2. Gateway timeouts + auth retries. Metrics show 502s up ~18x starting ~08:12PT. Customers calling in. Creating incident thread.
support-bot: automated alert: Hosted inference gateway (usw2-edge) latency p50/p95 elevated; 502 spike detected; correlated with egress errors. Pager sent to oncall.

sophia: oncall here. looking at gateway cluster logs and LB health. no deploys in the last hour. can anyone share network telemetry from the edge?

nate: I grabbed quick MTR / tcpdump from a coloc node in usw2-a. mtr shows intermittent loss on the egress hop toward Provider-N1:
```
Host: api-gw.usw2.redwood.net
Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
 30.0%   20   12.3  15.6   1.2  120.5  34.2
```

tcpdump snippet: lots of retransmits and repeated TLS handshake retries -> upstream resets. Not seeing backend model hosts failing; this looks like egress path instability where the gateway talks to upstream peering.

marina: AcmeCorp just opened a SEV1 ticket, they reported 502s across multiple regions for calls routed to us-west. Customer impact: production inference timeouts and billing webhook failures. They asked for ETA.

alex: repro (from our synthetic):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-hosted-small","prompt":"test"}'
# response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\n{ "error": "upstream read timeout" }
```

reliability-bot: No gateway deployment events detected in the window. Autoscaling events: several target deregistrations from the NLB due to healthcheck failures around 08:13-08:18PT (likely symptomatic).

sophia: triage notes: 1) gateway -> provider egress showing packet loss and retransmits 2) TLS handshake retries causing auth middleware to return 502s 3) backend model services remain healthy. immediate mitigations: enable smart-routing fallback to secondary egress peer, and shift high-tier customers to dedicated path. nate, can you request alternate BGP path or community from provider?

nate: opened ticket with Provider-N1 NOC — they acknowledged an as-path change and short maintenance window causing transient packet loss on their peering. Requested BGP community to prefer alternate transit. Also pushing to fail traffic to Provider-N2 for the problematic PoP. Estimated propagation ~5-10min after policy change.

marina: should we surface interim status to customers? AcmeCorp wants billing hold until resolved.

alex: do not auto-pause billing. Offer credit if they were impacted >5m. Marina please draft a support/status update: short, factual, estimated ETA.

marina: draft status: "Investigating elevated 502s/timeouts for us-west hosted inference. Root cause appears to be a transient egress network disruption with our peering provider. We are routing traffic to an alternate peer; service restoration in progress. Will update within 15 minutes." ok to post?

sophia: yes post that. also add note about potential increased latencies during the shift. set customer-facing incident id INC-20260317-USW2.

nate: provider confirmed route change applied at their edge; I pushed a local policy to prefer Provider-N2 for the affected PoP. Observed packet loss drop from ~30% -> ~1% within ~4 minutes.

alex: after failover: gateway 502 rate decreased to baseline (~1.2x) and auth retries normalized. monitoring shows p95 latency back to normal in ~6 minutes. keeping this thread open to monitor for 30m and then RCA.

sophia: immediate action items: 1) follow up with provider for full incident timeline and BGP logs 2) capture tcpdump/mtr for RCA 3) run a canary of heavy customers through dedicated path to validate stability 4) prepare credit calculations for impacted customers

marina: AcmeCorp rep confirmed recovery and asked for RC timeline. I'll schedule a handoff to AMs and support engineers for credit workflow.

reliability-bot: follow-up reminder scheduled: 30m. No further deploys. Archive incident once provider provides confirmation.

sophia: last update: traffic shift completed at 08:54 PT, 502s fell back to baseline by 09:00 PT. monitoring in passive mode. If no regressions, we'll close and prepare RCA with provider logs.

alex: thanks all — tracking RCA and billing notes. assigning postmortem to @sophia and @nate. close when RCA draft uploaded.
